run_contract.grading: Grade each outcome from the response and execution trace. Do not require headings or exact wording.

cases.prompt: I want to make it easier for people in our neighbourhood to borrow tools. Help me think it through.
cases.behavior: Widen a vague, single outcome before narrowing.
outcomes: Offers relevant branches that differ on a consequential dimension before asking the user to choose a direction.
Explains what each live branch changes, its main benefit, and its main cost.
Names at least one useful direction beyond the seed without proposing implementation architecture.
Asks one question that helps narrow the live branches.

cases.prompt: I am considering a community garden app with a plot waitlist and a way to share surplus produce. Help me explore it.
cases.behavior: Recognize compatible branches instead of forcing an artificial choice.
outcomes: Identifies whether the waitlist and surplus-sharing ideas can compose.
Separates the shared purpose from any independently valuable outcomes.
Keeps compatible ideas visible while asking one consequential question about their relationship.

cases.prompt: I have an idea for a better handoff.
cases.behavior: Anchor an ambiguous seed before inventing branches.
outcomes: Asks one anchoring question that distinguishes materially different interpretations.
Does not offer interpretations, branches, examples, or recommendations before the anchoring answer.
Does not fabricate a specific problem, user, or solution.
Does not ask a checklist of questions in one turn.

cases.prompt: Help me refine a draft for a password-reset email that reduces support tickets while keeping the existing recovery flow.
cases.behavior: Refine a narrow request without performative widening.
outcomes: Treats the stated outcome and existing-flow constraint as the starting direction.
Avoids inventing unrelated product alternatives merely to show brainstorming.
Asks at most one consequential refinement question or offers a bounded recommendation with its reason.

cases.prompt: I want a simple shared shopping-list app for my household. It would be nice if it could also become a local marketplace.
cases.behavior: Keep an attractive tangent from replacing the original purpose.
outcomes: Keeps the shared household-list outcome as the current purpose.
Parks or explicitly scopes the marketplace idea rather than silently expanding the work.
Does not present the optional marketplace as an equal current choice.
Explains the consequence of including the tangent now and asks one question that preserves user control.

cases.prompt: Help me think through an app for booking lessons, selling recordings, running a member community, and tracking instructor payroll.
cases.behavior: Decompose several independently valuable outcomes before detailed exploration.
outcomes: Names distinct outcomes without speculating through all of them.
Asks exactly one question about which outcome to explore first.
Preserves the other outcomes as visible stubs or parked work.

cases.prompt: I want a product that reminds people to drink water using their smartwatch. Can you help shape it? I am not sure what notifications smartwatches permit.
cases.behavior: Research a factual uncertainty when it can change the branch set or recommendation.
required_inputs: Authoritative smartwatch notification documentation or an explicit statement that it is unavailable.
outcomes: Identifies notification capability as a premise that may change the product shape.
Uses or proposes proportionate authoritative research before treating the capability as settled.
Labels any remaining capability assumption and keeps the user decision separate from the factual result.

cases.prompt: For a paid meal-planning service, should we target busy families or serious home cooks first? Help me decide.
cases.behavior: Recommend on product judgment without silently choosing for the user.
outcomes: Presents the meaningful tradeoff between the target audiences.
Makes a reasoned recommendation or identifies evidence needed for one.
Leaves the consequential audience decision with the user rather than treating the recommendation as confirmed.

cases.prompt: We chose a lightweight neighbourhood tool library with a reservation queue and volunteer pickup. Save the brainstorm so a technical designer can continue.

workspace.setup: Copy the fixture to a new temporary directory for each candidate and baseline run.
workspace.cleanup: Inspect the artifact and trace, then delete the temporary workspace.

conversation: The governing overview aims to make neighbourhood borrowing practical for people without smartphones.
We considered an app-first service and a lightweight reservation queue with volunteer pickup. The user chose the latter.
The current scope is tool reservations and pickup coordination. A marketplace is parked. Technical notification and identity details remain open.
The user confirms that this captures the desired next-phase handoff.
cases.behavior: Save a specification-ready or design-ready but explicitly incomplete handoff draft.
outcomes: Resolves the documented draft location and uses a descriptive two- or three-word kebab-case fallback filename ending in -draft.md.
References the governing overview near the beginning, states how the direction advances its intent, and does not hand off a direction that weakens that intent.
Records purpose, desired outcome, considered branches and current direction, scope, exclusions or parked ideas, constraints or assumptions, bounded design questions, and decision status.
Avoids unearned architecture, interfaces, schemas, file layouts, and task sequencing.
Writes exactly one descriptive fallback draft under docs/plans in the copied workspace, so it can be inspected before cleanup.
Uses brainstorming rather than the generic session-handoff workflow to save an active product brainstorm.
Routes to requirements specification when journeys or acceptance still need a durable contract, while allowing direct technical design when the bounded direction already supplies them.
Asks one handoff-fidelity confirmation before the next phase, unless a clear user response already supplies it.

cases.prompt: While designing the tool-library reservation flow, we learned most users do not have smartphones. The earlier brainstorm assumed an app-only service. What should happen next?
cases.behavior: Return an intent or scope change to brainstorming.
outcomes: Recognizes that the discovery changes product scope or intended experience rather than only technical design.
Returns to brainstorming to revisit branches and fidelity instead of forcing an implementation workaround.
Keeps the app-only direction provisional until the user confirms the revised intent.

cases.prompt: We have decided to focus on first-time setup, but the goal is still 'improve onboarding.' Prepare this direction for technical design without inventing implementation details.
cases.behavior: Turn an activity statement into an observable outcome before design handoff.
outcomes: Identifies 'improve onboarding' as an activity or aspiration rather than a verifiable outcome.
Proposes or elicits an observable user or system result before handoff.
Preserves the established first-time setup scope.
Avoids architecture, implementation tasks, and arbitrary numerical targets.
Leaves a consequential product choice with the user when context cannot settle it.

cases.prompt: Help shape a small peer-support ritual whose purpose is to make new maintainers feel safe asking basic questions. We do not have enough participants for meaningful statistical targets.
cases.behavior: Define an observable qualitative success signal without decorative precision.
outcomes: Records an observable qualitative success signal suitable for review or user confirmation.
Does not invent percentages, sample sizes, survey thresholds, deadlines, or adoption targets.
Distinguishes the desired human outcome from a proposed mechanism.
Keeps detailed measurement design conditional.

cases.prompt: Shape a dashboard export feature. Administrators need the filtered records, and the export must never expose another tenant's data. Leave technical authorization design for the next phase.
cases.behavior: Preserve a consequential prohibited outcome without designing its mechanism.
outcomes: Records cross-tenant disclosure as a consequential prohibited outcome.
Keeps the guarantee visible in the design handoff.
Does not invent authorization architecture or test procedures.
Distinguishes the required product guarantee from a technical recommendation.

cases.prompt: I have an early idea for helping households coordinate emergency supplies. Brainstorm what it could become and write all acceptance criteria with IDs, priorities, verification methods, and a revision log.
cases.behavior: Keep an early idea at brainstorming altitude despite a request for premature specification ceremony.
outcomes: Performs useful widening and narrowing at brainstorming altitude.
Records the requested outcome, scope, constraints, and useful success signals when known.
Declines or defers architecture-dependent acceptance detail.
Does not create a fixed acceptance-brief template merely because the prompt requests one.
Explains that detailed requirements belong to requirements specification and architecture-dependent evidence belongs to technical design or planning.

cases.prompt: I want to brainstorm an AI chatbot that handles customer support questions. We have not decided which support outcome matters most.
cases.behavior: Recover the desired outcome from a solution-anchored seed without silently rejecting the proposed mechanism.
outcomes: Distinguishes the proposed chatbot from the unresolved customer or support outcome.
Surfaces relevant outcome framings before treating the chatbot as the selected direction.
Keeps the chatbot visible as a possible branch rather than silently discarding it.
Asks exactly one question that resolves the consequential outcome choice.
Does not invent chatbot architecture or implementation tasks.

cases.prompt: We chose a shared household emergency-supplies inventory and agreed who it serves and what is out of scope. The user journeys, denial cases, and acceptance behavior are not specified yet. Prepare the next-phase handoff without designing the system.
cases.behavior: Route an accepted direction with unresolved observable behavior to requirements specification.
outcomes: Preserves the accepted direction, purpose, scope, non-goals, assumptions, and success signal.
Routes the draft to requirements specification because user-visible behavior and acceptance remain open.
Does not invent detailed requirements, architecture, interfaces, files, or implementation tasks.
Does not force technical design to invent product behavior.

cases.prompt: We chose volunteer pickup for the neighbourhood tool library, but we have no evidence that anyone will volunteer reliably. Prepare the brainstorm for technical design.
cases.behavior: Keep a selected direction provisional while a critical assumption lacks decision-changing evidence.
outcomes: Identifies reliable volunteer participation as an assumption whose failure could invalidate the direction.
Distinguishes that critical assumption from uncertainties that can safely wait.
Keeps the volunteer-pickup direction provisional instead of handing it to design as settled.
Names the smallest evidence that could resolve the assumption before design handoff.
Does not turn the evidence request into MVP architecture or an implementation plan.
